Dream. Prepare. Succeed.
Enquire Now
Explore our school and see our vibrant learning environment in action.
Welcome to Heath House Preparatory School
A co-educational prep school for children 3-11 years in Blackheath, London.
A family-run establishment since 1993, we pride ourselves on creating a nurturing and stimulating environment where every child can achieve their full potential.
Our Unique Outlook on Education
We believe in preparing children not just for academic excellence, but for life. Our holistic, engaging, and thorough teaching methods foster a love of learning, ensuring that our pupils are well-rounded individuals prepared for global success. Heath House pupils leave with the skills and confidence to excel in any learning environment, embodying our belief that a happy child is a learning child.
Heath House is not just a school, but a community.
VAT ON SCHOOL FEES
The school has decided to absorb the cost of applicable VAT on tuition fees and not pass it on to the parents.
Why Choose Heath House
Excellent Inspection Results
Our latest ISI inspection report highlights our commitment to high academic and ethical standards. In all areas, we were judged to be "Excellent,” the highest possible rating. The report praised our pupils strong literacy skills, moral understanding, and extensive extracurricular activities​. Read More
Outstanding Academic Success
Our pupils consistently excel in their 11+ exams, a testament to our exceptional teaching and individual education plans. We ensure personalised attention by keeping our class sizes small. Read More
Unified School Community
At Heath House, we believe in the power of teamwork. Our dedicated teachers and supportive parents work in partnership, creating a cohesive and understanding environment. This unified front is crucial in helping our pupils thrive academically and personally. Read More
Top Destinations For Leavers
Our pupils consistently secure places at top Independent and Grammar schools, both in the UK and internationally. At Heath House, our rigorous academic preparation ensures that every child is equipped with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to excel in their next educational steps. Read More

Mark Pearce

Blackheath Village’s rich background provides our pupils with unparalleled educational opportunities. From local museums, galleries and historical sites, as well as daily access to the expansive Heath, our pupils benefit from a curriculum that extends beyond the classroom, fostering a well-rounded and culturally enriched education.

Welcome to Heath House Preparatory School, where our unwavering commitment to academic excellence and personal development, forms the cornerstone of our educational philosophy. About Heath House Preparatory School
Heath House Preparatory School is a co-educational prep school for children aged 3–11 in Blackheath, London. Since 1993, our small classes, nurturing ethos and high expectations have helped pupils develop confidence, character and strong academic foundations for 11+ and beyond. Set across three close-by buildings in Blackheath Village, we offer a close-knit community where every child is known, supported and challenged. Our most recent Independent Schools Inspectorate review confirms that we meet all requirements and highlights our inclusive culture, robust safeguarding and well-planned curriculum.

A happy, purposeful school where curiosity, hard work, respect and resilience drive excellent learning—inside the classroom and through sport, the creative arts and rich co-curricular opportunities.

Our History
Home |
Our History
Established in 1993, Heath House is a co-educational independent preparatory school for children aged between 3 and 11 years.
Located in the heart of Blackheath Village, SE3, the school comprises three buildings, with two annexes to its main building in Wemyss Road: Tranquil Hall, the original village school building (1851) and The Old Library in Blackheath Grove. Heath House is an accredited member of the Independent Schools Association (ISA) and is inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI).
History and Milestones
Since opening its doors in 1993, Heath House has grown from a single building to a multi-site institution, deeply integrated into the historic and vibrant community of Blackheath. Our commitment to providing exceptional education has led to the expansion of our facilities and curriculum, offering enriching experiences both locally and abroad.

Creative Curriculum
Home |
School Life|
Creative Curriculum
Art & Design
Art at Heath House encourages creativity and self-expression as pupils experiment with different mediums and techniques, drawing inspiration from famous artists such as Frida Kahlo, William Morris and Pablo Picasso to name a few. The children create flick paintings; build sculptures; demonstrate knowledge of angles, symmetry and geometry to produce a geometric animal for example; mix oil pastels and colours; paint abstract pictures and create collages. Our Design projects enable pupils to develop practical skills by planning, designing, and creating their own models and structures whilst improving their fine motor skills.
Performing Arts and Music
The curriculum includes Music and Drama as key subjects. All Heath House pupils take part in the Trinity College London Graded Exams (Musical Theatre/Poetry and Prose). In addition, our pupils have the incredible opportunity to perform on stage at the historic Greenwich Theatre, where they perform a musical production in the Summer Term. Another highlight of the curriculum is the Gym & Dance display, which is held at the Blackheath Halls. This is a wonderful showcase of the children’s hard work and the skills they have learnt through their weekly Gym & Dance lessons.
The Heath House curriculum also includes weekly Music lessons, which all pupils participate in from Kindergarten to Prep Year 6. Pupils have the opportunity to use a range of musical instruments, including guitar, piano, drums, percussion, recorder and ukulele while learning musical theory.

Educational Visits
Heath House children enjoy a huge variety of day trips throughout the school year. Recent workshops and visits include: Houses of Parliament, Royal Courts of Justice, Sky Studios, Centre of the Cell, the Royal Institution, King's College University of London, London Zoo, Dulwich Picture Gallery, V&A Museum of Childhood, Science Museum, Natural History Museum, and many more. You can read more about these trips in our academics page, as we include this as part of our curriculum. Beyond the curriculum, Heath House offers a range of opportunities for further enrichment.
Community Outreach
Community is at the core of the Heath House values. Our pupils and staff regularly participate in community outreach events. Our pupils often litter pick in the local area. We also participate in Jeans for Genes day, where pupils are encouraged to wear Jeans to school and donate £2 to Genetic Disorders UK. The school hosts a variety of charity events throughout the year, including the Big Toddle - a short, sponsored walk for children under five for Barnardos, NSPCC Bobble Hat Day, foodbank workshops and so much more. One of our most beloved traditions is at Christmas time, where the Upper School students (Prep 5 & 6) go to Morden College and sing for the elderly residents. Details of community events and more can be found on our calendar and social media.
Residential Trips
All trips offered at Heath House are action packed, educational and most importantly great fun for the children. There are age and number limits on some of the trips with priority given to the Year 6 pupils. These trips are at additional cost.
Overseas Trips
Scotland Trip
PGL Multi-Activity Trip
Overseas Trip
Heath House has previously organised a week long Classics trip to Greece or Italy. Children from Years 3 to 6 have Classics as part of their History timetable. They receive a good foundation in the civilisation and culture of ancient times. The Classics trips are a unique opportunity to visit the sites and relics that the children have studied in class. It becomes much more real when they are actually running round the original Olympic stadium in Olympia, for example, visiting the Parthenon in Athens, or equally marvelling at Michelangelo’s work on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel and visiting Mount Vesuvius! These are just a few of the many experiences of these Classics trips.
Scotland Trip
The trip is essentially an adventure trip, based in the Royal Borough of Tain near Inverness in the Scottish Highlands. Children visit places in the Scottish Highlands where they have the opportunity to watch salmon leaping, go on an outdoor highland adventure walking in the hills with a highland ranger, go dolphin and seal sighting, and take a tour of Dunrobin Castle. The children also have the chance to view a fantastic falconry exhibition, tour the Inverness Caledonian Thistle football club, visit RAF Tain to observe at close range RAF fighter planes practising, take a trip to Cromarty to play on the beach, explore Landmark Activity Park, visit the cinema, go bowling and much more!
PGL Multi-Activity Residential Trip
PGL is the UK’s leading provider of school trips and children’s adventure holidays – offering outdoor education and adventures of a lifetime to children since 1957.’
PGL offers a wide range of residential courses across the UK, designed to stimulate, educate and motivate primary school pupils. Encouraging team building and leadership skills, the multi-activity residential courses combine fun and personal development in a lively and supportive environment. They keep the pupils busy from breakfast to bedtime with a huge variety of land and water based adventure activities. Mornings and afternoons are each split into two sessions so that children can experience up to four different outdoor activities each day. By extending them socially, physically and mentally, a Multi-Activity course gives the children far more than simply academic achievement by which to measure themselves. Heath House takes children every year on a 2 night, 3 day PGL trip either to Wiltshire or Sussex.

Early Years Foundation (Age 3-5)
Academics
Kindergarten School
Leading Kindergarten School in London, UK
At Heath House, our kindergarten school is where children begin their learning journey with confidence, curiosity and a genuine love of school. Welcoming children from age 3 into our Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), we provide a warm, structured and engaging start that balances play, exploration and early academic foundations. Kindergarten and Reception form our EYFS, based in Tranquil Hall, where children feel safe, known and encouraged to try new things every day.
Our approach is personal: children benefit from individual attention and thoughtfully planned activities that support early communication, independence and positive friendships—while gently introducing the skills they’ll need for a smooth transition into Reception and beyond.
Age: 3+
Setting: Tranquil Hall (EYFS)
What children gain in Kindergarten
Language & confidence through conversation, storytelling and sharing
Independence through routines, responsibility and self-care skills
Friendships & social skills through cooperative play and kindness
Early writing readiness through mark-making and fine-motor development
Early number sense through hands-on, practical Maths
Kindergarten Curriculum at Heath House, London
As a private kindergarten school, Heath House follows the EYFS framework for children aged 3 to 5 (Kindergarten & Reception), delivered in a nurturing environment at Tranquil Hall. Our EYFS curriculum places a strong focus on Literacy and Maths, while also supporting the wider areas that build confident, well-rounded learners. Learning in Kindergarten is hands-on and meaningful. Children build early reading and writing readiness through stories, talk, role play and mark-making, while number skills develop through practical activities that help children understand quantity, patterns and problem-solving. Every child’s progress is carefully supported so they feel proud of what they can do—and excited about what comes next.

Subjects for Kindergarten
In our london kindergarten school, children enjoy a rich and varied curriculum from the very start. From age 3, pupils are introduced to a broad range of subjects, taught in age-appropriate and engaging ways: English, Maths, French, Science, Geography, History, R.E, Computing, Music, Drama, Art & Design, Mandarin, Physical Education, and PSHE & RHE.
This breadth matters because it gives children language, ideas and experiences to talk about, explore and create. Alongside classroom learning, Heath House draws inspiration and depth from the resources of London, helping children connect their learning to the world around them.

Why Choose Heath House Kindergarten School?
Families choose Heath House because children are supported to thrive academically and personally in an environment that is both purposeful and kind. Our Early Years setting provides calm structure and meaningful learning while building the foundations children need for a confident transition into Reception and beyond.
The Heath House difference
From the first term, we aim to develop happy, confident learners who feel secure at school, enjoy friendships, and are excited by discovering new things every day.
Confidence-building routines that develop independence and resilience
Kindergarten School Admissions
Kindergarten school admission at Heath House begins with an informal parental visit, followed by an interaction with the headteacher. Children may join the Kindergarten class after their third birthday, and parents can apply at any time until the class becomes full.
Once a place is offered, parents receive the required forms. The Registration Form, Medical Form and Home School Agreement are returned to the school alongside the £200 registration fee and a £1,800 confirmation deposit. For children aged seven and above, admissions also include an informal assessment in English, Mathematics and Non-Verbal Reasoning.

Community Connection
Home |
Beyond Heath House|
Community Connection
Community Outreach
Community is at the core of the Heath House values. Our pupils and staff regularly participate in community outreach events. Our pupils often litter pick in the local area. We also participate in Jeans for Genes day, where pupils are encouraged to wear Jeans to school and donate to Genetic Disorders UK. The school hosts a variety of charity events throughout the year, including the Big Toddle - a short, sponsored walk for Lower School children in support of Barnardo's, NSPCC Bobble Hat Day, Foodbank workshops and so much more. One of our most beloved traditions is at Christmas time, where the Upper School pupils (Prep Year 5 & 6) go to Morden College in Blackheath and sing carols for the elderly residents. Details of community events and more can be found in our school diary dates and social media pages.

pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care
Home |
School Life|
Pastoral Care
Our School Values
The school has strong values that are used as a tool to maximise the pupils’ potential and welfare.
These values are
These values are interwoven into all aspects of school life.
Respect
Tolerance
Individual Confidence
Good Manners
Resilience and Grit
Sportsmanship
Kindness
Responsibility
British Values
The school’s values support the children’s understanding of the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance for those with different faiths and beliefs, and are taught throughout the curriculum, in age-appropriate ways. Heath House staff take on the responsibility of ensuring these values are actively promoted to children, and evident in every curriculum and enrichment aspect of school life.
School Rules
The School Rules are simple, and based on safety, consideration and responsibility. The School Rules are displayed on notice boards throughout the school and staff should display a copy in their classroom. The School Rules are also displayed in each child’s journal. The School Rules can be seen below.
Our School Rules
Be honest.
Always have your reading book with you.
School Captains
School Council
School Houses
Eco Council
School Captains
As part of teaching the British Values and encouraging democracy, pupils elect two School Captains and two Vice Captains. This is announced in the Awards Ceremony at the end of the Summer Term. The captains are chosen from pupils in Prep Year 6. The School Captains carry out important jobs on behalf of the School. Amongst other things, they act as role models to the younger children, are encouraged to take initiative to organise charitable fundraising days and speak at school events.
School Council
The Heath House School Council is a group of elected children who discuss issues raised by their peers which helps to effect change within the school. For example, introducing new clubs or making changes to the lunch menu!
The School Council meets once a week. Two pupils are elected as Heads of School Council, who chair the meeting. Elected members from Prep Year 3 upwards discuss issues raised by their peers throughout the week.
School Houses
Eco Council
Safeguarding
At Heath House, safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility and promoting the welfare of children is of paramount importance. Class teachers support and monitor each child’s wellbeing using a holistic approach, reporting any concerns to the school’s Safeguarding Team.
The school has robust policies and procedures in place to support the safeguarding of all pupils. All staff ensure that they are aware of the policies and procedures and attend regular safeguarding training.
Children are taught, in an age appropriate manner, to have an awareness of potential dangers that they may face, including whilst online. In addition to this children are encouraged to develop trusting relationships with their teachers which allows for open communication about any worries or concerns the child may have.
Should you have any safeguarding concerns please contact the Designated Safeguarding Team on [email protected]/heathhouse_uk

Welcome to Heath House Preparatory School
A co-educational prep school for children 3-11 years in Blackheath, London.
A family-run establishment since 1993, we pride ourselves on creating a nurturing and stimulating environment where every child can achieve their full potential.
Our Unique Outlook on Education
We believe in preparing children not just for academic excellence, but for life. Our holistic, engaging, and thorough teaching methods foster a love of learning, ensuring that our pupils are well-rounded individuals prepared for global success. Heath House pupils leave with the skills and confidence to excel in any learning environment, embodying our belief that a happy child is a learning child.
Heath House is not just a school, but a community.
VAT ON SCHOOL FEES
The school has decided to absorb the cost of applicable VAT on tuition fees and not pass it on to the parents.
Why Choose Heath House
Excellent Inspection Results
Our latest ISI inspection report highlights our commitment to high academic and ethical standards. In all areas, we were judged to be "Excellent,” the highest possible rating. The report praised our pupils strong literacy skills, moral understanding, and extensive extracurricular activities​. Read More
Outstanding Academic Success
Our pupils consistently excel in their 11+ exams, a testament to our exceptional teaching and individual education plans. We ensure personalised attention by keeping our class sizes small. Read More
Unified School Community
At Heath House, we believe in the power of teamwork. Our dedicated teachers and supportive parents work in partnership, creating a cohesive and understanding environment. This unified front is crucial in helping our pupils thrive academically and personally. Read More
Top Destinations For Leavers
Our pupils consistently secure places at top Independent and Grammar schools, both in the UK and internationally. At Heath House, our rigorous academic preparation ensures that every child is equipped with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to excel in their next educational steps. Read More

Mark Pearce
Welcome to Heath House Preparatory School, where our unwavering commitment to academic excellence and personal development, forms the cornerstone of our educational philosophy.

The Global Schools Advantage
The Global Knowledge Exchange Programme involves interaction between teachers and pupils from partner schools around the world, exposing them to global best practices and educational standards. By integrating technology to enhance learning outcomes and nurturing good manners and social skills, the programme fosters respectful and well-behaved pupils.
Prime Location in Blackheath Village
Blackheath Village’s rich background provides our pupils with unparalleled educational opportunities. From local museums, galleries and historical sites, as well as daily access to the expansive Heath, our pupils benefit from a curriculum that extends beyond the classroom, fostering a well-rounded and culturally enriched education.
